The Impact of Healthfulness on Firm Performance

The Case of Food Companies in South Korea
Suh, Y., S. Lee, S. Jung, D. Jung, & W. Yun
Journal of Product Research, 39(4), 57-65
2021
Published (KCI Indexed)

Abstract

This study examines the relationship between product healthfulness and firm performance in the South Korean food industry. Using a comprehensive dataset of food companies and their product portfolios, we investigate how health-oriented product strategies impact various dimensions of firm performance, including financial metrics, market positioning, and consumer perception. Our findings provide insights into the business value of health-focused product development strategies.

Research Motivation

🏥 Growing Health Consciousness

The global trend toward health-conscious consumption has fundamentally transformed the food industry landscape:

  • Increasing consumer demand for healthier food options
  • Rising awareness of diet-related health issues
  • Government initiatives promoting public health through nutrition
  • Growing premium placed on functional and organic foods

📈 Business Strategy Question

Despite the apparent consumer preference for healthy foods, the business implications remain unclear:

  • Mixed evidence on whether health-focused strategies improve financial performance
  • Potential trade-offs between healthfulness and profitability
  • Limited understanding of market positioning benefits
  • Need for empirical evidence in the Korean market context

Theoretical Framework

🎯 Resource-Based View

Health-oriented capabilities as strategic resources that can provide sustainable competitive advantage through differentiation and value creation.

📊 Signaling Theory

Healthfulness as a quality signal that reduces information asymmetry between firms and consumers, potentially commanding premium prices.

🌱 Stakeholder Theory

Health-focused strategies as means to satisfy multiple stakeholders including consumers, regulators, and health-conscious investors.

Methodology

🗂️ Data Collection

Comprehensive analysis of South Korean food industry:

  • Sample: 156 publicly listed food companies (2015-2019)
  • Product Data: Nutritional information and health claims from product portfolios
  • Financial Data: Revenue, profitability, market share, and stock performance
  • Market Data: Consumer perception surveys and brand positioning metrics

📏 Key Measures

Healthfulness Index:

  • Nutritional profile scoring (calories, sugar, sodium, fiber content)
  • Functional ingredient presence (probiotics, omega-3, vitamins)
  • Health certification and claims (organic, low-fat, sugar-free)
  • Portfolio composition (proportion of healthy vs. conventional products)

Performance Metrics:

  • Financial: ROA, ROE, Revenue Growth, Profit Margins
  • Market: Market Share, Brand Equity, Customer Loyalty
  • Innovation: R&D Investment, New Product Success Rate

🔬 Analytical Approach

  • Panel Data Regression: Fixed effects models controlling for firm heterogeneity
  • Instrumental Variables: Addressing endogeneity concerns in strategy-performance relationship
  • Mediation Analysis: Understanding mechanisms linking healthfulness to performance
  • Robustness Checks: Alternative specifications and sensitivity analyses

Key Findings

💰

Positive Financial Impact

1-standard deviation increase in healthfulness index associated with 12% higher ROA and 8% revenue growth.

🏆

Market Premium

Health-focused companies command 15-20% price premiums and achieve 25% higher brand equity scores.

📈

Long-term Benefits

Healthfulness effects strengthen over time, with cumulative benefits emerging after 2-3 years of consistent strategy.

🎯

Moderation Effects

Benefits are stronger for smaller firms and in competitive market segments with high health awareness.

Detailed Results

📊 Financial Performance

Return on Assets (ROA): +12.3%
Revenue Growth: +8.7%
Profit Margins: +5.2%

🎯 Market Performance

Brand Equity: +25.1%
Price Premium: +18.4%
Customer Loyalty: +14.6%

🔬 Innovation Metrics

R&D Investment: +22.8%
New Product Success: +16.3%
Patent Applications: +19.7%

Managerial Implications

🎯 Strategic Planning

Health-oriented product strategies should be viewed as long-term investments that require sustained commitment and integration across business functions.

💼 Product Development

Invest in R&D capabilities for functional ingredients and nutritional enhancement while maintaining taste and affordability.

📢 Marketing Strategy

Develop authentic health positioning backed by credible certifications and transparent communication about nutritional benefits.

🏢 Organizational Capability

Build cross-functional teams spanning R&D, marketing, and operations to ensure coherent health-focused value proposition.

Policy Implications

🏛️ Public Health Policy

Results suggest that market-based incentives can effectively promote healthier food production. Policymakers should consider:

  • Supporting health-focused innovation through R&D tax incentives
  • Strengthening nutritional labeling requirements for transparency
  • Promoting public-private partnerships for health education

⚖️ Regulatory Framework

Balanced regulation that promotes innovation while ensuring consumer protection:

  • Clear guidelines for health claims and functional food classification
  • Streamlined approval processes for genuinely beneficial health innovations
  • International harmonization of health standards for trade facilitation
